verdict: PACCAR's revenue rose 19% to $7.9 billion and profit jumped 44% as truck margins recovered sharply and its record Parts business kept delivering steady earnings.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue $7.94B, up from $6.67B a year ago

kpis.label: Parts revenue
kpis.note: A quarterly record, with $404M of pretax profit

kpis.label: Truck deliveries
kpis.note: Global deliveries, up from 31,900 a year ago

segments.name: Truck
segments.note: Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF trucks — sales jumped 28% as fleets refreshed vehicles, and truck pretax profit more than quadrupled to $455M.

segments.name: Parts
segments.note: Replacement parts for trucks on the road — a record quarter, and the most profitable piece per dollar of sales ($404M pretax).

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.note: Loans and leases that help customers buy trucks, shown net of $5M of intersegment eliminations; pretax profit was $138M.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing next-generation trucks, including clean diesel, hybrid and battery-electric models.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Dealers support, sales and running the company — $125M in Truck/Parts plus $43M in Financial Services.

otherDetail: Other income of $111M: $84M of investment income plus $27M of net interest and other income in the truck business.
footerNote: Adaptation: the cost stage combines the truck business's cost of sales ($6,311M) with Financial Services' funding costs ($350M) and its $29M provision for loan losses, so the flow balances to PACCAR's reported totals. Operating income here is a derived subtotal — PACCAR reports pretax income of $1,081M, which equals the $971M operating figure plus $111M of other income.

takeaways.title: Truck profits snapped back
takeaways.text: Net income rose 44% to $848M, driven by truck segment margins: Truck pretax profit jumped to $455M from $103M a year ago on 28% higher truck sales.

takeaways.title: Parts set another record
takeaways.text: Parts revenue hit a record $1.78B with $404M of pretax profit — a steady, high-margin business that cushions PACCAR when truck sales swing.

takeaways.title: Fleets are buying again
takeaways.text: Global deliveries rose to 40,100 trucks from 31,900, and PACCAR expects healthy U.S. Class 8 demand to continue into 2027.
